inventory.label: the heron feather
inventory.notes: Day 5 paid back partially: the feather's slow walk and head-up posture turned out to be exactly the gait for tracking — YY read the fox's exit trail off the scratch-pine and used it to locate her abandoned crevice cache. The constraint that has been costing him meals is starting to teach him a different way of foraging.

inventory.label: a single rust-colored kit-tuft
inventory.notes: Caught on the lip of a stone on the rocky shoulder, at the entrance to the fox's old den. Tells YY: the fox left with kits, not alone — meaning she went looking for a den with more cover, meaning she will not be back to this slope this season. Useful information; not food. YY brought it home anyway.

identity_notes: Late winter — YY ate the kernel on the spot and is still hungry but no longer falling.
Yesterday: watched the beechnut cluster travel away; noticed a deer track in the surge mud.

Today: smelled the absence at the scratch-pine and used the feather-walk (slow, head up) to read the fox's exit trail. Found her old den, a tuft of kit-fur on the stone lip, and one whole hickory kernel in a low crevice she had missed.
Standing thread: the feather-walk is starting to be its own kind of forage. The fox left with kits — she is not coming back to this shoulder.
